lines.en: Theo, look at this park! We used to play here all day, and our parents never worried about where we were.
lines.pt: Theo, olhe este parque! A gente costumava brincar aqui o dia todo, e nossos pais nunca se preocupavam com onde estávamos.

lines.en: I remember. We used to ride our bikes until the streetlights came on, and I did not use to wear a helmet.
lines.pt: Eu lembro. A gente costumava andar de bicicleta até as luzes da rua acenderem, e eu não costumava usar capacete.

lines.en: Neither did I! My brother used to be very shy, but he would climb that big tree without any fear at all.
lines.pt: Nem eu! Meu irmão era muito tímido, mas subia naquela árvore enorme sem nenhum medo.

lines.en: Did you use to play football with the older kids? I think they used to chase us away from the field.
lines.pt: Você costumava jogar futebol com os mais velhos? Acho que eles costumavam nos expulsar do campo.

lines.en: Yes, and we used to build a secret fort behind the bushes. It was our headquarters, and nobody else knew about it.
lines.pt: Sim, e a gente costumava construir um forte secreto atrás dos arbustos. Era nosso quartel-general, e ninguém mais sabia.

lines.en: There used to be an ice cream truck here every Sunday. Now there is only a coffee stand and a new playground.
lines.pt: Costumava ter um caminhão de sorvete aqui todo domingo. Agora só tem uma barraca de café e um parquinho novo.

lines.en: Times have changed. Children spend more time on their phones, so the park is quiet and almost empty.
lines.pt: Os tempos mudaram. As crianças passam mais tempo no celular, então o parque é tranquilo e quase vazio.

lines.en: True, but I think we were lucky. I used to hate going home, because the evenings were so much fun.
lines.pt: Verdade, mas acho que tivemos sorte. Eu odiava ir para casa, porque as noites eram muito divertidas.

lines.en: I used to dream about living in a place like this, with trees, a lake and a long path to run on.
lines.pt: Eu costumava sonhar em morar num lugar assim, com árvores, um lago e uma trilha longa para correr.

lines.en: And now you do! You live five minutes away, so you can bring your daughter here on weekends, just like we used to.
lines.pt: E agora mora! Você vive a cinco minutos daqui, então pode trazer sua filha nos fins de semana, como a gente fazia.

lines.en: Good idea. I will teach her to climb that tree, and maybe she will build a fort of her own.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Vou ensinar minha filha a subir naquela árvore, e talvez ela construa um forte só dela.

facts.label: Hábitos do passado
facts.sub: used to + infinitivo; did + use to.

facts.label: sujeito + used to + infinitivo
facts.sub: Use para hábitos que acabaram: We used to play outside all day. A pronúncia é “iús-tu”. Pode ser traduzido por “costumava”.

facts.label: did + use to
facts.sub: Com did, o verbo volta para use: Did you use to play? I did not use to wear a helmet. O d do used some porque did já marca o passado.

pages.title: We used to play outside · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm afternoon in Austin. Tess walks into the old park. Children shout. A bike leans against a tree. Theo arrives with two ice creams. They sit on a bench.

“Theo, look at this park! We used to play here all day, and our parents never worried about where we were.” says Tess. “I remember. We used to ride our bikes until the streetlights came on, and I did not use to wear a helmet.” says Theo. “Neither did I! My brother used to be very shy, but he would climb that big tree without any fear at all.” says Tess.
